name: localfold
description: WebGPU protein structure prediction in the browser - AlphaFold 2 (monomer and multimer), AlphaFold 3, ESMFold2 and OpenDDE
//: A published package AND this repository's dev manifest. Nothing here is needed to open the page or run the CPU tests: `files` ships shared/, cpu/ and webgpu/ only, and everything under devDependencies belongs to one of the optional lanes below.
//peerDependencies: Dawn's node binding, for `localfold/node` only - a browser caller brings its own GPUDevice and needs nothing installed. 0.6.0's linux-x64 prebuilt wants GLIBC 2.38; use 0.4.0 below that.

scripts.//test: --js-float16array is asked for ONLY when this node lacks Float16Array and its V8 lists the flag, so a node that already ships the type and a node too old to know the flag both run unchanged. Without it twelve tests do not fail, they never RUN - see CLAUDE.md.
scripts.test: node $(node --v8-options 2>/dev/null | grep -qe '--js-float16array' && node -e 'process.exit(typeof Float16Array === "undefined" ? 0 : 1)' && echo --js-float16array) --test --test-concurrency=1 $(ls test/*.test.js | grep -v '\.gpu\.')
scripts.//test:gpu: Needs a Dawn that loads on this glibc AND the fixtures under test/fixtures/evoformer/, which are gitignored - 24 of them are ENOENT on a fresh checkout. tools/gpu-chrome.mjs is the lane that works here; see CLAUDE.md, including the create() toggles these 25 call sites do not pass.
scripts.//test:stock: The configuration a VISITOR has: no shader-f16 and no subgroup matrix units, which is every NVIDIA Chrome. Two of the four models did not fold here at all - see docs/A100.md. Needs the bundles, like the other GPU lanes.
scripts.//test:browser: playwright.config.js is the config - testDir test/browser, and it starts `python3 -m http.server 4173` itself. It still needs a browser: `npx playwright install chromium`. Without one it is 4 failed on 'Executable doesn't exist'.
scripts.//typecheck: ADVISORY, not a gate: 1075 errors on this tree. It checks JS against @webgpu/types and most of what it reports is missing DOM and window augmentation rather than anything a fold would notice.
scripts.//test:template: Every model's TEMPLATE moves its fold, on a target that needs one. Both oracle checkers for this stage drive the module with templates: 1 where a FOLD pads to four, so a wrong denominator is exact in every module check and a quarter strength in every fold - which is what rosettafold3 was. 5CAJ chain A, with and without.
scripts.test:smiles: node tools/check-smiles-vs-rdkit.mjs && node tools/check-stereo-vs-rdkit.mjs && node tools/check-smiles-rewrites.mjs && node tools/check-smiles-conformer.mjs
scripts.//test:affinity-mw: G4 - does this port's molecular weight agree with RDKit's, which is the one upstream computes affinity_mw with? The weight feeds Boltz-2's molecular-weight correction, so it reaches a log10(IC50) a reader ranks on. 🔴 IT FOUND THE TABLE WRITTEN FROM IUPAC 2021 WHERE RDKit SHIPS AN OLDER ONE - 51 of 86 elements disagreed, and the correction's three coefficients were FITTED against RDKit's values, so being more correct than them is the bug. Needs the dump: python3 tools/oracle/dump_rdkit_molwt.py
scripts.//test:affinity-quant: G1 - is the affinity bundle's float32Tensors list actually protecting its norms? 🔴 quantize_af3.py's KEEP_FLOAT32 regex is SLASH separated and the affinity export carries upstream's DOT separated PyTorch names, so it matches none of them and only the manifest's own list keeps a LayerNorm scale out of int5. Decodes the shipped bundle on the host and requires the protected groups EXACT; --falsify empties the list, re-quantises and requires them to degrade. Needs the two export directories.
scripts.//test:affinity-oracle: G2 - does the float64 affinity reference compute upstream PyTorch's function, seam by seam? 🔴 THE ORACLE IS f32 BECAUSE UPSTREAM'S TRIANGLE EINSUM FORCES IT (torch.chunk(x.float(), ...)), so the bound is a measurement and the gate carries a 9-mutation separation control. 🔴 AND PAIR SEAMS ARE COMPARED ONLY WHERE BOTH TOKENS ARE LIVE: a fully masked attention row is -1e9 on every key, f32 spacing there is 64, so the logits collapse to uniform where f64 keeps them - different garbage in a region nothing downstream reads. Needs the dump: python3 tools/oracle/dump_boltz2_affinity.py
scripts.//test:affinity-contract: Does LocalFold's OWN AF3 pair kernel set accept Boltz-2's affinity weights? The whole GPU port rests on this, so it is measured rather than argued: triangle multiplication, grid attention BOTH directions and the transition at both factors, against the float64 affinity reference. 🔴 THREE TENSORS' ORIENTATIONS DIFFER BETWEEN PyTORCH AND AF3 AND ARE NOT SHAPE ERRORS - q/k/gate are (out, channels) and v and the output projection are (channels, out), linear_o being square - so each is re-run with the other layout and must disagree. Needs only the f32 export.
scripts.//test:affinity-gpu: G3 - does the GPU affinity pairformer compute the float64 reference's answer? AGENTS.md requires a deterministic differential for every GPU kernel. 🔴 IT FOUND THE INCOMING TRIANGLE'S a/b ORDER REVERSED, which the host contract gate could not see because its reference is outgoing-only: tri_mul_out exact at 1.0e-7 while tri_mul_in read 0.304. 🔴 AND PAIR SEAMS ARE COMPARED ONLY WHERE BOTH TOKENS ARE LIVE - the GPU runs f32 and reproduces upstream's uniform logits in a fully masked row where the f64 reference does not, so comparing padded rows would fail a correct kernel. Needs the f32 export symlinked as /model-boltz2-affinity-f32.
scripts.//test:affinity-keys: G6 - does the affinity stack collide with the trunk in ONE pipeline cache? 🔴 THE SHAPES ARE IDENTICAL: AF3's trunk grid attention is 128 channels / 4 heads / 32 dimension and so is the affinity pairformer, so the only things separating their keys are swapTransposedBias and the staged precision - and CLAUDE.md records two collisions that were exactly a key not naming a constant its shader embeds. Bundle-free, because a collision is a property of keys and sources rather than of weights being real, and check-pipeline-key-collisions.js rightly refuses with one bundle. Both orders, plus a sensitivity control so the reuse count cannot be blind.
scripts.//test:affinity-crop: Does the affinity crop select the tokens upstream's AffinityCropper does? An EXACT index-set comparison - the crop either keeps a token or it does not - over 12 cases that reach all three break conditions (the loop ends in `break`, not `continue`, so each budget truncates at a different place). 🔴 A res_stride case is deliberately absent: it HANGS upstream, whose grow loop has no exit when the window holds fewer tokens than the neighbourhood - unreachable from real input, but the port guards it. Needs: python3 tools/oracle/dump_affinity_crop.py --boltz=<checkout>
scripts.//test:affinity-forward: Does the GPU affinity module compute the WHOLE function - the pair LayerNorms, the projections, the broadcast sum, the distogram, the conditioner, the stack, the pooling and all three heads - against upstream's own dump? G3 covers the pairformer; this covers the number a reader ranks on. 🔴 The float32 glue is written independently of cpu/af3/affinity/ on purpose: sharing it would compare those stages with themselves. Pair seams live-only, outputs whole. Needs the G2 dump and the f32 export, both symlinked under the served root.
scripts.//test:affinity-sinputs: Does upstream's `affinity=True` substitution reach `s_inputs`, and ONLY through the profile? `targetFeat` IS Boltz's s_inputs - buildTargetFeat sums an atom-encoder output, a restype one-hot, the MSA profile and the deletion mean at 384 channels (token_s) plus boltz2's targetFeatSum - and affinity=True changes exactly the profile and the deletion mean for their depth-1 variants. Asserts it MOVES, moves only where the deep profile is not already a one-hot, and equals the no-alignment batch's. 🔴 It does NOT compare against upstream's own embedder; that needs its whole featuriser and is named open in the tool's header.
scripts.//test:affinity-project: Does the fused pair LayerNorm+projection kernel compute the host's answer? AGENTS.md requires a differential for every GPU kernel; the reference is written in the gate rather than imported, because the two host implementations that exist are what this kernel REPLACES. Both real shapes (128->128 and 256->128) plus a ragged 130->100. 🔴 Its falsify input carries rows whose variance is the SIZE of eps, because the `1/sqrt(v+eps)` convention is invisible at variance ~1 AND at variance exactly 0 - the control MISSED it twice before the input could express it.
scripts.//test:boltz2-featurise: Does this port's batch agree with UPSTREAM BOLTZ's own featuriser? A reference this port did not have: test:batch compares against AF3's dump, which is af3-any-model's featuriser - the thing this port derives from - so an error the two AF3-side implementations SHARE is visible here and nowhere else. 🔴 The atom layouts diverge (flat windows against DENSE-24), so what is compared is every quantity whose meaning survives the re-layout: the token fields, the disto and CENTRE slots, and ref_space_uid as a PARTITION. Needs: python3 tools/oracle/dump_boltz2_featurise.py --boltz=<checkout> (which needs numba; no CCD and no mols.tar).
scripts.//test:affinity-memory: G7 - does the screening loop leak GPU memory across ligands? The test:switch failure in a screen's shape: ten models in one page went 677 -> 1281 -> 2171 -> 2874 MiB and the fourth fold died. 🔴 TWO PHASES, because "memory grew" is not a leak when the ligands differ in size: `repeat` folds ONE ligand N times so every shape is identical and any growth at all is the loop holding something, and `varied` folds N sizes where the bound is one ligand's worth. 🔴 ITS CONTROL IS --pooling=off AND NOT --free=off: the per-ligand drain moves nothing on this path (every AF3-side allocator but WebGpuExecution's destroys at release), so that arm cannot vary the thing under test, while the allocator's own pooling switch reproduces the failure at 492 MiB a ligand. Needs the int5 bundle and the f32 affinity export symlinked.
scripts.//test:screen-page: Does the SCREEN PAGE work - the controls a reader touches, not the API? 🔴 CLAUDE.md records three bugs that survived every API-path run because a UI path cannot be seen from one: a SMILES box whose blur handler turned benzene into hexane, setChains deleting the ligand row, and a contact row coming back as A:SGB:C. So this types into the ligand box, fires its events, presses Screen and reads what is DRAWN - the table rows, the scatter circles, py2Dmol's own viewer registry - then builds the archive in the page and reads it back through readZip. 🔴 IT CAUGHT TWO ON ITS FIRST RUN: uniqueIds returns IDS and not entries, so every job was id undefined; and py2Dmol owns #status and had silently overwritten the page's own status line. Needs both bundles symlinked locally.
scripts.test:no-webgpu: python3 tools/screen-in-page.py --page=bench.html --no-webgpu && python3 tools/screen-in-page.py --page=bench.html --no-webgpu --as-ua=linux && python3 tools/screen-in-page.py --page=bench.html --no-webgpu --as-ua=windows && python3 tools/screen-in-page.py --page=screen.html --no-webgpu
scripts.test:no-adapter: python3 tools/screen-in-page.py --page=bench.html --no-adapter --as-ua=linux && python3 tools/screen-in-page.py --page=bench.html --no-adapter --as-ua=windows && python3 tools/screen-in-page.py --page=bench.html --no-adapter
scripts.//bench:g8: G8 - this port's affinity NUMBERS against upstream Boltz running the same job, which is the one thing every other affinity gate cannot see: they compare a FUNCTION to a FUNCTION on identical input, and the number a reader ranks on comes out of the COMPOSITION. 🔴 IT CANNOT BE A TOLERANCE TEST: the affinity is read off a SAMPLED pose, so upstream disagrees with itself seed to seed and a hand-picked bound would measure the author's optimism. The gap between the means is reported in units of UPSTREAM'S OWN seed-to-seed spread, which is the control. 🔴 Seeds are NOT paired across implementations - seed 0 in PyTorch is different noise - so rows are never differenced. NOT a CI gate: upstream runs on CPU here, minutes a seed, and needs 6.1 GB of its own assets (../tools/fetch_boltz_cache.sh).
scripts.//test:boltz2-method: Is boltz2 folded with the method conditioning class genuine Boltz-2 uses? 🔴 IT WAS NOT: this port fed class 1 (X-RAY DIFFRACTION) where upstream feeds 4 (OTHER / THEORETICAL MODEL), which is what a de novo prediction is - and that one constant moved a predicted IC50 by a factor of 2.2. 🔴 NO PER-TOKEN DIFFERENTIAL COULD SEE IT: the method row is a learned 384-vector added IDENTICALLY to every token, so it shifts target_feat wholesale rather than distorting any token, and it survived a target_feat agreement at 1e-8 against af3-any-model because that port feeds class 1 too - two implementations wrong together. Only bench:g8, against the checkpoint's own authors, could find it. Part of npm test; fails 3/3 with the fix reverted.
scripts.//test:site: Assembles dist/ and runs build_site.py's own unresolved-import check. 🔴 THE ONLY GATE THAT SEES A CONSTRUCTED PATH. The src/ reorganisation broke five python tools that build paths from segments - (ROOT / "src" / "reference" / "manifests" / "index.js") - where no literal path exists for any pattern to match, and test/imports-resolve.test.js found none of them. Run this after any move under src/.
scripts.//check:safari: Parses every shipped module with this Mac's system JavaScriptCore, the engine of its Safari. Syntax an older Safari cannot parse (regex lookbehind before 16.4, class static blocks) fails the whole module at load, before any code runs. macOS only; skips elsewhere. See docs/RFD4P-FROM-LOCALDESIGN.md.
scripts.//check:python: Does every python tool run on the OLDEST python3 a developer here has (3.9, Apple's /usr/bin/python3 on the M2)? Every python gate in this file is spelled `python3 <tool>`, so the version is the machine's - and a tool needing 3.10 dies in a `def` line with a TypeError about `|`, which reads as a bug in the tool. build_site.py did, so `npm run test:site` was broken on that Mac. The twin of check:safari, for the other interpreter this repository is run with.
scripts.//test:delta: Does the shipped uploader ADD a delta to weights that are already resident? AlphaFold 2 is five models and a bundle is 97 MiB where a delta is 43; this holds `planBlockUpload(..., { accumulate: true })` to ZERO differing f16 results on real AlphaFold tensors, with two controls - the same plan with the flag off must DIFFER, and the result must land nearer the model the delta names than the base does. Needs the base and delta bundles on disk; see tools/pack_delta_model.py.
scripts.//test:pending: A result belongs to the model that made it: switching the model row veils the structure and the map and takes the confidence numbers away, rather than leaving the previous model's answer under the new model's name. It borrows python/localfold/server.py as a FIXTURE to get a prediction onto a page without weights, and measures the veil as pixels.
scripts.//test:tools: Every tool has a header line saying what it is, and docs/TOOLS.md lists exactly the tools that exist with exactly those lines. 🔴 44 TOOLS WERE NAMED BY NOTHING AT ALL - not CLAUDE.md's table, not docs/, not another tool - including working differential checkers. The index is DERIVED from each file's own header, so an entry cannot drift from it; regenerate with `python3 tools/index-tools.py --write`.
